name: PA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+17 partisan lean anchors the race heavily toward the incumbent party
Reschenthaler holds a dominant financial edge, raising $4.9M to Bradstock's $0.37M
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 3%, with no polls or expert ratings signaling competitiveness
model.rationale: The R+17 lean, Reschenthaler's overwhelming fundraising advantage, and markets pricing the Democrat at roughly 3% all point the same direction, and no polls or expert ratings offer any counterweight. Bradstock's modest $370K war chest is respectable for the district but nowhere near enough to overcome the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any credible public polling showing the incumbent under 60% in a strong Democratic national environment would be the first sign of a shift worth monitoring.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwestern Pennsylvania's 14th District sits firmly in Republican territory with a partisan lean of R+17, and incumbent Guy Reschenthaler is seeking another term after clearing his primary. His campaign has raised about $4.9 million with $741,000 on hand, dwarfing Democrat Alan Bradstock's $370,000 raised and $64,000 in cash. No outside groups have invested meaningfully on either side, another sign the race is not viewed as competitive.

No public general-election polling or expert race ratings are available, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which give Bradstock only about a 3% chance. A favorable national climate for Democrats would need to be historically large to put this seat in play, and nothing in the available evidence suggests it is. The incumbent remains a heavy favorite.
